text:
Stellantis Sinks 8% as Q3 Report Nears; Ford Drops 4%, General Motors Slides 3%
Stellantis shares are cratering ahead of a quarterly report that management already warned would be seasonally weak, and Ford and General Motors are getting dragged down with it. Whether next week's results steady the sector or deepen the rout depends…
Selling is sweeping through automaker stocks, and Stellantis N.V. (NYSE:STLA | STLA Price Prediction) shares are taking the biggest damage as the company’s Q3 2026 report approaches next week. Stellantis shares have dropped 8%, recently at $3.94, leaving the stock 64% lower year to date (YTD).
Meanwhile, Ford Motor (NYSE:F) stock is down 4% to $11.47. General Motors (NYSE:GM) shares are down 3% to $74.91, showing the pressure spans the automakers.
The Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR ETF (NYSEARCA:XLY) is down 2% to $113.07, while the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is down 0.7% to $758.94. Thus, the aforementioned automotive stocks are trailing both the consumer discretionary sector and the overall market.
Stellantis Bears the Brunt of the Auto Selloff
Stellantis hasn’t issued a guidance change or operational update that would account for the decline. Recent company releases center on product and brand news for Jeep, Dodge and Mopar, along with a Q3 sales report. With peers falling and earnings approaching, the move fits a sector pullback heading into results.
A day earlier, Stellantis and Alumobility, an aluminum industry association, presented a joint study finding that an aluminum-intensive design could cut vehicle weight and allow a smaller battery with the same driving range. The findings are theoretical.
Stellantis Carries a Different Risk Profile Than Ford and General Motors
Stellantis earns much of its profit from Jeep and Ram in North America, and it also runs a large European business. Ford and General Motors are more concentrated in the U.S. market, which leaves Stellantis managing a wider set of regional challenges. Management highlighted pricing pressure in Europe on the Q2 2026 earnings call, and the region posted an adjusted operating loss for the quarter.
Stellantis’s margins remain the weak spot. In Q2, the automaker posted a 1.8% adjusted operating margin. Progress showed up elsewhere, with Stellantis swinging to a net profit from a year-earlier loss and North America sales growing 6% in a fourth consecutive quarter of gains.
As of June 30, the consumer discretionary fund held Ford at 1.4% and General Motors at 1.7% of net assets. Stellantis didn’t appear among its disclosed holdings, so the fund’s drop draws on a much wider mix of retail, travel and restaurant stocks.
On the upside, management expects Stellantis’s savings program to deliver €6 billion of annual run-rate cost reductions by 2028. The downside case centers on its credit profile, after S&P downgraded Stellantis to BBB- and Moody’s cut it to Baa3.
Stellantis Turnaround Heads Into Its Q3 Test
Stellantis’s third-quarter report next week may show whether its turnaround plan is gaining working. Joao Laranjo, the finance chief at the time of the Q2 call, stated that “Q3 will be impacted by the summer shutdown and continued raw material inflation.” Management expects Q4 2026 to benefit from higher volume and a stronger ramp of cost-saving initiatives, and it has reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance for mid-single-digit revenue growth along with positive industrial free cash flow in 2027.
An open variable for Ford and General Motors is the tone of automaker trading once Stellantis reports. The question is whether the XLY consumer discretionary fund keeps lagging the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust as earnings season moves through the sector.
A large YTD loss already weighs on Stellantis heading into a quarter management called seasonally weaker. Solid results could ease that pressure, while another soft quarter might extend the slide. Investors should consider keeping their position sizes modest until sentiment turns positive on STLA stock.
